purpose: Track objective contract events that can affect availability, transaction risk, role security or late-season incentive behavior. Contract status alone must never directly boost fantasy projections.
source_priority: 1. Official NFL/team transaction or contract announcement
2. NFL.com / AP / Reuters / ESPN / CBS contract reporting
4. Reputable fantasy/beat reporting for watchlist discovery only; re-verify before model action

three_state_incentive_rule.PARTIAL_PUBLIC: Money or existence is verified but exact threshold is not.
three_state_incentive_rule.UNKNOWN: No verified public incentive details found. UNKNOWN must never be interpreted as NONE.

projection_guardrails: Never add fantasy points because a player is merely in a contract year.
Use contract data primarily for alerts: hold-ins, trade risk, extension completion, no-tag clauses, roster guarantees, and explicit incentives.
A performance incentive can affect the model only when the exact threshold is verified, the threshold is realistically reachable, and remaining game context makes deliberate usage plausible.
Even then, treat incentive proximity as a small context modifier; observed routes, carries, targets, snaps, red-zone work, opponent strength and game environment remain primary.
When a contract is extended, automatically clear contract-pressure flags without waiting for a manual preseason list refresh.
For defensive/OL stars, contract disputes matter only when they change participation, availability or transaction probability; then re-run opponent matchup projections.
